what: The machine-readable half of the P1-28 closing package. It names ONE commit as the phase's code candidate and records every measurement taken against it, with the provenance of each. docs/phase-1/phase-1-28/evidence/closure-evidence.md is the prose half and must state the same candidate; scripts/ci/build-p1-28-evidence-manifest.mjs refuses a disagreement between the two.
why: P1-27 shipped a closing page that pinned a head 47 commits behind the tree it described, and it went on reading like evidence because nothing compared the claim with the repository. A closing value that names no head is not a measurement of anything. Every figure below therefore carries the head it was taken at and the artefact it came from.
whatThisIsNot: This is not a tamper-proof seal and not a hosted observation. The digests in evidence-manifest.json remove SILENT revision, not revision. The hosted figures were collected from the GitHub API by a reader of the run; this file records them with their run, job and artefact ids so a later reader can fetch the same objects and disagree.

candidate.subject: merge: browser-tier determinism — the tier was rate-limited by the product's own limiter
candidate.whatFreezingMeans: Every figure in this package describes THIS commit. Commits that land after it are docs-and-machinery successors and are listed in `successors` below; each is required to leave apps/** and supabase/** byte-identical, so the product these measurements describe is the product at the candidate. A successor that changes either tree invalidates this package and the candidate must be re-frozen and re-measured.
candidate.productIdentityExpectation: empty output — no product file differs between the candidate and any successor
candidate.vocabularyNote: `FINAL_CODE_SHA` and `FINAL_CODE_TREE` are the names this package was commissioned under and are used here so the commissioning brief and this record cannot drift apart. They are NOT the P1-27 spelling: that phase says `CODE_CANDIDATE_SHA` for the same idea, and no file in this repository used `FINAL_CODE_*` before this one. The mapping is recorded below rather than left for a reader to guess, because two names for one commit is exactly how a superseded head gets quoted as a current one.

vocabularyMapping.FINAL_CODE_SHA: P1-27 calls this CODE_CANDIDATE_SHA — the newest commit touching any non-document path.
vocabularyMapping.FINAL_CODE_TREE: The tree object of that commit. P1-27 records no equivalent field; it is added here because a tree id is what makes two checkouts comparable without trusting a commit message.
vocabularyMapping.EVIDENCE_RECORD_SHA: P1-27's name for the commit carrying the evidence file — here, each entry in `successors`.
vocabularyMapping.EXECUTABLE_DIFF_COUNT: P1-27's derivation `git diff --name-only CODE_CANDIDATE_SHA..EVIDENCE_RECORD_SHA` excluding docs/ and *.md. DOCUMENTATION_ONLY_RECORDING may be claimed only when it is exactly zero. This package does NOT claim DOCUMENTATION_ONLY_RECORDING for its first successor, and says so in `successors[0]`: that commit adds executable evidence machinery. It claims the narrower and checkable thing instead — that apps/** and supabase/** are byte-identical, so the PRODUCT measured is the product at the candidate.

successorRule: Every commit in `git log 38afa5c2..HEAD` that touches an EXECUTABLE path — anything outside `docs/` that is not `*.md` — must appear below by its full 40-character id, and `build-p1-28-evidence-manifest.mjs` computes the range and refuses an unnamed one. A DOCUMENTATION-ONLY successor may go unnamed, and the gate prints the ones that did: a commit cannot write its own id into a file it contains, so 'the list is exactly `git log`' is not a rule any repository can satisfy. That is the one hole, it is exactly one commit wide, and it is reported rather than hidden.

successors.what: P1-28-QA-005 itself: the evidence manifest generator and its gate, the gate's test, the command-register entries, the hosted-job wiring, and the two documents of this package. It adds no file under apps/** or supabase/** and changes none, so the measured product is the candidate's.
successors.why: The packaging of a candidate cannot be inside the candidate it packages; a manifest that digested itself would have no fixed point, and a package written before the run it reports could not name the run.

successors.what: The seal's own test corrected to check each local tier against the head it names rather than against the other tier's head, plus the P1-27 local run ledger re-recorded, its closing values reconciled and its evidence package resealed.
successors.why: check-p1-27-closing-values.mjs expires a local run record when any executable path changes since it was taken. The machinery commit above is such a change, so the record is re-taken rather than left to describe a head it no longer describes. This commit touches `tests/ci/p1-28-evidence-manifest.test.ts`, so it is executable and is named here rather than treated as documentation.

howTierFiguresAreChecked: Three obligations, because there are three kinds of claim. ARITHMETIC: `passed + failed + skipped` must equal the declared total, for every tier — the review set `passed: 3, failed: 812` beside `tests: 2475` and the first revision of the gate accepted it, because nothing added the three numbers up. LOCAL: the figures must equal the P1-27 run ledger's, read out of git at the commit named in `localLedger.atCommit`, and a LOCAL tier may carry no figure the ledger does not write — `suites` stood here for a whole revision and came from nowhere a reader could reach. HOSTED: cannot be computed from this repository at all, and the gate says so in those words; what it requires instead is that the claim be FETCHABLE — a run id, a job id, the head the job ran at, and the artefact — so a later reader can retrieve the same object and disagree.

unit.label: root unit and foundation

localLedger.howChecked: `git show ab5e3c49:docs/phase-1/phase-1-27/evidence/local-run-ledger.json` — the ledger AS IT STOOD when this measurement was taken, not as it stands now. Pinned to a commit because the ledger MOVES: `check-p1-27-closing-values.mjs --record` rewrites it at whatever head it was last taken at, so a check against the working copy would go red on the next unrelated re-record and would then be relaxed rather than fixed.

unit.note: The local record was taken at cae8bdb0, an ancestor of the candidate. That no EXECUTABLE path differs between cae8bdb0 and the candidate is now COMPUTED by the gate rather than asserted here — the whole diff is two P1-27 evidence documents. A READER RUNNING THE SUITE TODAY WILL SEE A LARGER NUMBER, and that is not drift: the successors above add QA-005's own gate test, so the ledger has since been re-recorded at a later head and reports a bigger unit tier. This figure is frozen at the candidate on purpose, which is exactly why it is checked against a PINNED ledger rather than the current one. `suites: 549` used to sit here and has been removed: the ledger records no suite count, so nothing could ever have checked it.

browserByProject.howTaken: Read per test entry out of the run's own playwright-report.json, grouped by `projectName` and the owning spec file. NOT inferred from a keyword count and not copied from a local run.
browserByProject.note: The tablet project observes this phase at 1024x768 (apps/web/playwright.config.ts:254-260). Its testMatch at :255 names `(administration|appointments-and-receptions)`, so the P1-28 surface is seen at two viewports and two locales. Documents written before the tablet merge (88af8acd / 4c6ccfe7) said this tier ran no P1-28 screen at a tablet viewport; that was true when written and is false at this candidate.

hostedCi.howTaken: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/38afa5c28e5b78d484a442cf6b8596fb2a5c34aa/check-runs — the per-commit endpoint, because /actions/runs does not list every check.

codeql.whatThisDoesNotProve: A CodeQL run on a pull request is DIFF-INFORMED. Two analyses at this head each returned 0 results and the repository carries 0 open alerts on any analysed ref, but a pull-request analysis does not by itself establish the repository ceiling; only a run on a protected ref does. This is recorded as the pull-request result it is.

database.note: database-migration-replay applies all 120 migrations to an empty database and records the resulting schema hash; hosted-clean-room re-applies them at the exact SHA and re-derives the same 1356-cell RLS matrix independently.

FE-007.blocker: G-EMP / R6 — Owner register question A
FE-007.owner: the Product Owner, with the contract half owned by P1-18
FE-007.whatIsStillOpen: The receiving-employee REFERENT. The wizard writes receiving_employee_id on every check-in while the column has no foreign key and no defined meaning. The UUID-on-screen defect this row used to carry is FIXED — both read-back surfaces resolve the name through iam.user-detail and never print the identifier — so what remains is an Owner question about what the column means, not a Frontend defect.

FE-012.blocker: P1-OD-025 — document and media file policy, with G-MEDIA / R8 behind it
FE-012.owner: the Product Owner (the decision) and P1-15 / P1-18 (the contract half)
FE-012.whatIsStillOpen: The damage-map half. damage_map requires a registered documentId AND the exact documentVersionId, and neither value can exist while the document-category table is empty, no storage provider is configured and no version can be accepted. The mark write itself is delivered and proved — exact coordinates, unrounded, keyboard-placeable, clamped at the contract bounds.

FE-018.blocker: P1-OD-025 — document and media file policy; and the unowned signature read-back gap
FE-018.owner: the Product Owner (P1-OD-025); P1-18, unassigned (the read-back gap)
FE-018.whatIsStillOpen: rec.reception-signature is called ZERO times by the product. The write needs a registered document and its exact version and nothing in this product registers a document. What ships states what a signature would attribute and records nothing, with the absence of a submit control asserted so it cannot creep back.

P1-28-OD-001.title: who administers the intake catalogues, and through which surface
P1-28-OD-001.whatMustBeDecided: (a) WHO administers the intake catalogues — a tenant administrator, a head-office role, or the platform operator; and (b) THROUGH WHICH SURFACE — a screen inside this product, a separate administration application, or provisioning performed outside the product altogether.
P1-28-OD-001.consequenceToday: Seven intake catalogues ship zero rows and no screen in this product can add one. Two of those tables sit on a REQUIRED foreign key of an operator path — appointmentTypeId on apt.appointment-create and cancellationReasonId on apt.appointment-cancel — so until a catalogue is populated no appointment can be booked and none can be cancelled.
P1-28-OD-001.whatShipped: The API capability and nothing in apps/web. PR #227 registered 21 catalogue-management writes behind apt.catalogue.manage / rec.catalogue.manage; no seed grants either code to any role, so the capability is held by nobody. All 21 are recorded DELIBERATELY_ABSENT against this decision in docs/phase-1/phase-1-28/write-reachability.json, and check-p1-28-write-reachability.mjs resolves that reference against the §7 headings, so the classification cannot be entered with a fabricated decision id.
P1-28-OD-001.identifierCaveat: P1-28-OD-001 is an id in this phase's own namespace, following the P1-26-OD-### and P1-27-OD-### precedent. It is NOT a P1-OD-### allocation. If the Owner records this decision, the number the Owner assigns supersedes it.

ownerAcceptance.rule: The permanent Frontend closure rule from P1-26 onward: no Frontend phase closes without the Product Owner testing the running application in real installed Chrome and returning `OWNER ACCEPTANCE: PASS` verbatim. Silence is never Pass. Automated CI is necessary and is not sufficient.
ownerAcceptance.howToRun: npm run acceptance:serve — a production build, never dev:all. A dev stack compiles route bundles lazily and the API authenticator is installed as a side effect of composing the IAM module, so an acceptance session on a dev stack reports product defects that do not exist.
ownerAcceptance.note: This package is the technical evidence an acceptance session rests on. It is NOT a closure record and does not close the phase.
